title: Waves in the ionosphere plasma
caption: In a plasma ω² = ω_p² + c²k², so for a wave of frequency f the wavenumber is real only above the plasma frequency. For the ionosphere (n = 10¹² m⁻³) f_p ≈ 9√n Hz = 9 MHz: the curve starts at 9 MHz and climbs towards the vacuum line f = ck/2π. Shortwave below 9 MHz has no propagating solution and reflects; FM at 100 MHz is far above the curve's start and passes through.
alt: Graph of frequency in megahertz against ck/2π in megahertz: a hyperbola starting at 9 MHz when k is zero and approaching the straight line f = ck/2π, which is the vacuum relation.
description: The horizontal axis is ck/2π in megahertz (the frequency a wave of that wavenumber would have in vacuum); the vertical axis is the frequency f in megahertz.
The plasma curve is f = √(f_p² + (ck/2π)²) with f_p = 9 MHz, from the lesson's ionosphere example.
At k = 0 it starts at f_p = 9 MHz: no wave of lower frequency propagates, so shortwave radio below this reflects. At ck/2π = 12 MHz, f = 15 MHz.
Far above f_p the curve approaches the dashed vacuum line f = ck/2π, so VHF and FM waves pass through.
